definition.def: An interval between two events or dates is the period of time between them.
examples: The ferry service has restarted after an interval of 12 years. [+ of]
There was a long interval of silence.

definition.def: An interval during a film, concert, show, or game is a short break between two of the parts. [mainly British]
examples: During the interval, wine was served.
England were two goals behind at the interval.

definition.def: In music, an interval is the difference in pitch between two musical notes. [technical]
If something happens at intervals, it happens several times with gaps or pauses in between.
examples: She woke him for his medicines at intervals throughout the night.

definition.def: If things are placed at particular intervals, there are spaces of a particular size between them.
examples: Several red and white barriers marked the road at intervals of about a mile.
The trees which gave the road its name stood at regular intervals along the kerb.
At intervals there were red warning lights.

examples.sentence: Plyometric exercises help athletes make the best use of this brief interval.

The cosmic significance the Egyptians placed in the 12 decans led them to develop a system in which each interval of darkness (and later, each interval of daylight) was divided into a dozen equal parts.
After the interval, we'll go to Australia for a piece by Ross Edwards, The Tower of Remoteness, according to Edwards.
One or two members of staff should remain in the foyer to prepare for the interval.
